queue_policy: Inbound Agent replies autonomously only for low-risk policy-passing categories with a connected provider. Known warm relationships, sensitive contexts, and unproven Instagram POST/runtime paths escalate or wait.

capture_readiness.no_fake_inbound_policy: Do not create lead records from imagined comments or DMs.

response_templates.draft: It is an AI receptionist for local businesses. It can answer calls, collect the caller name, number, what they need, and pass the details back so the owner does not lose the lead when they are busy or closed.
Here is the site: https://thecalltaker.com. It is still early, but the goal is simple: help local businesses stop losing calls when nobody can pick up.

Current public pricing is $97, $497, and $997+ depending on what the business needs. I would not want to guess the right fit from one message, but the simple version is for missed-call and after-hours capture.
response_templates.escalation_trigger: discount, custom quote, contract, payment term, or special promise

response_templates.draft: Yes, the basic fit is strongest where calls turn into jobs or appointments. For {segment}, the useful scenario is usually capturing who called, what they need, and how urgent it is when nobody can pick up. What type of call do you miss most often?
That is genuinely helpful. I am trying to make this feel local and useful instead of like generic AI spam. If you were explaining it in one sentence to a business owner, what would you say?
I can send you a simple demo path. What would be the most realistic call to test: missed estimate, after-hours call, new appointment, or urgent service request?
response_templates.escalation_trigger: asks for a meeting with Wallace or live custom setup
